rows.observation: European gas storage at 72% capacity, the lowest level for this time of year since 2011
research: "finding": "In early October 2026, EU natural‑gas underground storage was at approximately 72 % of capacity, the lowest fill‑rate for this time of year since records began in 2011.",

"importance": "The low storage level reduces the EU’s buffer against winter supply shocks, increasing the risk of price spikes and possible demand‑side curtailment if a cold winter accelerates withdrawals, especially alongside the planned full ban on Russian LNG imports from January 2027 and tight global LNG markets.",

"evidence": "EnergyRiskIQ live‑data snapshot (3 Oct 2026) showed 72.0 % fill (GIE/AGSI+ source); EnergyScan weekly tracker (6 Oct 2026) reported 72.83 % full, noting it was below the lowest level recorded for that date between 2017‑2025; GIE weekly status (28 Sep 2026) gave EU total storage at 71.16 % full; the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEFA) stated on 3 Oct 2026 that storage was about 72.4 % full, the lowest for this time of year since records began in 2011.",
"sources": [
"EnergyRiskIQ live-data snapshot (3 Oct 2026)",
"EnergyScan weekly tracker (6 Oct 2026)",
"GIE weekly status (28 Sep 2026)",
"IEFA report (3 Oct 2026)"

"context": "EU gas‑storage regulation normally requires 90 % fill by 1 Nov; for the 2026‑27 winter the target was relaxed to 80 % (with up to 4 percentage‑points flexibility). Summer‑season injections have been weaker than in prior years (≈30 % decline in injection volume 2022‑2025). Geopolitical factors—loss of Russian pipeline gas, curtailment of Qatari LNG, and Middle‑East tensions—have limited replenishment. The European Commission acknowledges the low levels but asserts the system should still meet winter demand, while flagging heightened vulnerability to extreme weather.",

"uncertainty": "Daily fill‑rates fluctuate with injections and withdrawals, so the “lowest since 2011” claim depends on the exact comparison method (calendar‑date vs. seasonal‑week). Reported percentages vary slightly (71 %–73 %) due to differing capacity definitions (working vs. total) and reporting lags. Forward‑looking projections (e.g., cold‑weather scenarios) are speculative and not part of the observed fact.",
"status": "supported"

rows.observation: Asian premium to Europe at all-time high
research: "finding": "The price spread between Asian LNG (JKM) and European natural gas (TTF) has widened to historically extreme levels, with Asia commanding a premium over Europe that reflects intensified competition for flexible LNG cargoes following Middle East supply disruptions. The JKM-TTF spread reached over 20 EUR/MWh per ACER, averaged USD 2.8/MBtu in March 2026 per the IEA, and hit $2.79/MMBtu per S&P Global, its widest since late 2021. This premium reversal signals a structural shift in global LNG trade flows, with Atlantic-basin cargoes being diverted toward Asia and away from Europe.",

"importance": "This premium reversal is critically significant because when JKM trades above TTF on an energy-equivalent basis, LNG producers systematically route Atlantic-basin cargoes to Asia rather than Europe, directly constraining European LNG supply. The widening spread could undermine EU storage filling efforts, exacerbate European gas price volatility, and threaten energy security at a time when Europe is phasing out Russian gas imports and faces potential supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict. The shift also reflects a broader realignment of global LNG trade flows, with profound implications for European energy security and Asian supply reliability.",

"evidence": "ACER reports the Asian premium reached over 20 EUR/MWh following the Middle East conflict. The IEA Gas Market Report Q2-2026 states the JKM-TTF spread flipped from a European premium of USD 0.9/MBtu in January-February to an Asian premium averaging USD 2.8/MBtu in March 2026, with JKM volatility surging close to 300%. S&P Global assessed the JKM-TTF spread at $2.79/MMBtu on December 6, its widest since December 31, 2021, while the JKM-NWE spread reached $3.385/MMBtu. Investing.com notes JKM futures trading near 38-40 €, about 5-6 € above TTF. The World Bank reports the Asian LNG benchmark surged 94% in March 2026. Global LNG Hub indicates JKM's premium over TTF rose to $2.7/MMBtu, its highest year-to-date, driven by robust Asian demand from China and India. Timera Energy confirms strong Asian LNG demand is driving a premium of JKM over European prices, signalling diversion of US and West African supply from Europe.",
"sources": [
"ACER (European gas wholesale markets, winter 2025-2026)",
"IEA Gas Market Report Q2-2026",
"IEA Gas Market Report Q1-2026",
"S&P Global Commodity Insights (via Reuters)",
"Investing.com - Luca Mattei analysis",
"Global LNG Hub",
"World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook",
"Timera Energy",
"European Gas Hub",
"ICE (Intercontinental Exchange)"

"context": "The Asian LNG premium over European gas prices has widened to historically extreme levels, driven by the Middle East conflict (including potential Strait of Hormuz closure), the loss of nearly 20% of global LNG supply, robust Asian demand growth, and intensified competition for flexible LNG cargoes. The EU's ban on Russian gas imports and Panama Canal congestion have further complicated trade flows. While European gas demand has softened, Asian markets have strengthened, reversing the European premium that prevailed in late 2024 and early 2025. The spread has fluctuated significantly, with some sources indicating a European premium at certain periods and others showing an Asian premium at others, reflecting the market's high volatility.",

"uncertainty": "The research contains some conflicting signals about the timing and persistence of the premium, with certain sources indicating a European premium at other periods (e.g., TTF surging $1.4/MMBtu above JKM in late 2024, and the European premium reaching $1.92/MMBtu in January 2025). The data includes forward-looking projections for 2026-2027 that may not reflect current market conditions. The exact magnitude of the premium varies across sources and measurement methodologies, ranging from $0.34/MMBtu to over 20 EUR/MWh depending on the benchmark and time period assessed. The claim of 'all-time high' is not uniformly confirmed across all sources, with some indicating the widest level since 2021 or early 2023 rather than an absolute record.",
"status": "supported"

rows.observation: US natural gas production growing but unable to meet winter demand spikes
